title: Rajab: the night journey remembered
hookLine: many recall the night journey and the gift of the five prayers

cards: Before dawn, at midday, in the afternoon, at sunset, at night. Five times a day, in kitchens and offices and the back rooms of shops, Muslims who keep the prayer stop what they're doing, face Mecca, and pray.
From outside, it can look like a heavy schedule. But the story Muslims tell about where those five prayers came from frames them differently. In that story they weren't handed down as a burden.
They were a gift, brought back from the ascent through the heavens. In the month of Rajab, many Muslims remember that journey.

teach.b: Seven weeks ago you read the verse that opens Surah Al-Isra: "Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far Distant Place of Worship".
That's the Isra, the night journey, from Mecca to Jerusalem. The hadith collections tell the rest, the Mi'raj, the ascent through the heavens.

Bukhari and Muslim describe the Prophet ﷺ meeting earlier prophets at each level, and then being given the prayer: fifty prayers a day. On his way down, he met Musa, who asked what he'd been given. Fifty, he said.
Musa told him: your people won't manage that. I've tried with people before you.

teach.h: MUSA: GO BACK AND ASK FOR LESS.
teach.b: Go back and ask for less. So he went back, and it was reduced. And back again, and again, Musa sending him each time, until it was five.
Musa said, go back once more. The Prophet said he was ashamed to ask again. And then, in the hadith, the word came: they are five, and they are fifty.

teach.h: FIVE IN THE DOING, FIFTY IN REWARD.
teach.b: Five in the doing, fifty in the reward. So Muslims who pray five times a day are, in the story's terms, carrying a gift that was made lighter for them, out of mercy, with Musa's help, and still counted at its full weight.
When did it happen? The Qur'an doesn't give a date. Many Muslims commemorate it on the twenty-seventh of Rajab.

But scholars differ on the date, and the early sources give several different months. Some communities hold gatherings that night; others don't mark it specially. What everyone shares is the prayers themselves.

how: Many Muslims commemorate the Isra and Mi'raj on the 27th of Rajab with talks, recitation and extra prayer, while others do not mark a specific night; the five daily prayers are understood to have been given during the Mi'raj.

games.q: you're coming down from the heavens with fifty prayers a day for your people. Musa stops you. what does he say?
o: your people won't manage that. go back and ask for less.
fifty is too few; ask for more.
games.why: go back and ask for less. it happened again and again until five, which God called five in the doing and fifty in reward.

practice: If you pray, choose the next of the five, and before you begin, remember where the story says it came from: the ascent, and the long back-and-forth to make it light enough. Then pray it as a gift.
If you don't pray, take these few minutes as your own time set apart, and notice what it feels like to stop.
